if_blocked: If stolen electronics (mobiles/laptops) were resold to local pawn shops or grey-market dealers, execute immediate recovery under BNSS Section 106 via entity_id pawn_shops_jewelers.

steps.title: Judicial Application for Restitution of Funds and Property
steps.description: Submit a formal investigation report and application under BNSS Section 503 before the jurisdictional Magistrate to release frozen seller payouts or refund balances back to the victim (or e-commerce platform), and return seized genuine merchandise to rightful owners.
required_evidence: Schedule of frozen bank balances and seized physical inventory
Complainant's verification report and indemnity bond for property release
Court order directing restitution of funds and release of recovered property
steps.condition_to_start: Fraudulent funds frozen in bank accounts or physical merchandise recovered during raids.
steps.condition_to_complete: Court issues formal restitution orders transferring money/property to complainants.
if_blocked: If counterfeit branded goods are seized, obtain an order from the Magistrate under Trademark Act / BNSS for supervised destruction of the infringing inventory after evidentiary logging.

dead_end_strategies.condition: The e-commerce fraud was conducted on peer-to-peer (P2P) classified platforms (e.g., OLX, Facebook Marketplace) using fake army/police identification, prepaid burner SIMs, and cash withdrawals via CSP/mule points.
suggested_actions: Examine the IMEI number of the phone used to upload the classified advertisement by requesting platform backend logs and running IMEI clustering across nationwide telecom operators.
Analyse the UPI VPA transaction history to identify other victims who transferred money to the same collection account, consolidating multiple complaints to map patterns.
Request the platform to immediately blacklist the advertiser ID, device fingerprint, and bank account mapping across their ecosystem.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigating SIM Swap & eSIM Hijacking Bank Account Takeovers
source: Synthesized from DoT/TRAI SIM replacement regulations, I4C cyber fraud SOPs, and police telecom investigation guides

steps.title: Victim Triage & SIM Deactivation Timeline Profiling
steps.description: Interview the victim to establish the exact timestamp when their mobile network signal suddenly disconnected. Secure screenshots of any preceding phishing SMS, missed calls from unknown numbers (used to keep line busy), and subsequent bank debit alerts received via email.
required_evidence: Victim's written statement detailing exact date and time of network loss
Complainant's bank account statement showing unauthorized withdrawals occurring after SIM deactivation
Copy of email alerts received from bank or telecom operator regarding SIM change
steps.condition_to_start: Victim reports sudden loss of mobile network connectivity followed by unauthorized bank account draining.
steps.condition_to_complete: Establishment of a precise chronological timeline linking SIM deactivation to unauthorized banking transactions.
if_blocked: If the victim's email account was also compromised to suppress SIM swap notification alerts, instruct them to recover email access and check the trash/deleted folder.

steps.title: Telecom Requisition of SIM Swap / eSIM Upgrade Dossier
steps.description: Issue urgent notices under BNSS Section 94 to the victim's Telecom Service Provider (Jio, Airtel, Vi). Demand the complete SIM replacement / eSIM upgrade dossier: Point of Sale (PoS) agent details, store location, application form, forged ID proofs submitted, and CDR/IMEI logs of the new SIM.
required_evidence: SIM replacement / eSIM upgrade application form and forged KYC documents submitted
Point of Sale (PoS) agent name, agency ID, store address, and employee details who processed the swap
IMEI number and CDR of the device where the newly issued SIM/eSIM was activated
IP address and OTP verification logs (if eSIM upgrade was initiated via online portal/SMS)
steps.condition_to_start: Mobile number confirmed to have undergone unauthorized SIM replacement or eSIM porting.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of complete SIM swap diagnostic dossier, PoS agent identity, and new handset IMEI from TSP.
if_blocked: If the TSP claims the swap was automated via SMS/IVR without human intervention, subpoena the SMS logs and IPDR session logs of the device that sent the porting request.

steps.title: Bank Server Login IP & Beneficiary Tracing Requisition
steps.description: Issue notices to the victim's bank to obtain internet/mobile banking access logs during the fraud window. Request IP addresses, timestamps, device fingerprints, and immediate freezing of transferred funds across beneficiary accounts under BNSS Section 106.
required_evidence: Banking login and fund transfer IP address logs with exact UTC/IST timestamps and NAT ports
Beneficiary account numbers, IFSCs, and fund distribution ledgers
Confirmation of debit freeze / lien marking on recipient accounts under BNSS Section 106
steps.condition_to_start: Unauthorized bank transfers occurred concurrently with SIM deactivation.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of detailed banking login IP logs and confirmation of fund freezing in destination accounts.
if_blocked: If funds were moved into cryptocurrency exchanges, immediately route freeze notices to entity_id vasp_crypto_exchange.

steps.title: Investigation & Interrogation of Point of Sale (PoS) Agent
steps.description: Summon and interrogate the telecom PoS retailer or store employee who processed the fraudulent SIM replacement. Examine store CCTV footage, verify if statutory biometric verification / photo matching rules were violated, and check for criminal collusion.
required_evidence: CCTV footage of the telecom retail store / PoS counter showing the individual who collected the SIM card
Original physical application form and thumbprint/signature registers from the PoS store
Written interrogation statement of the PoS agent explaining verification failures
steps.condition_to_start: PoS agent ID and store location identified from TSP SIM replacement dossier.
steps.condition_to_complete: Procurement of store CCTV footage and determination of whether the PoS agent was a co-conspirator or deceived by forged documents.
if_blocked: If the PoS store CCTV is overwritten or malfunctioning, seize the agent's personal mobile phone and CDR to check for communication with known cybercrime syndicates.

steps.title: ISP IPDR Tracing of Bank Attackers and eSIM Hijackers
steps.description: Analyse the IP addresses obtained from bank login logs and online eSIM portal requests. Issue notices to ISPs to obtain IPDR, NAT port binding records, and subscriber installation addresses.
required_evidence: IPDR logs resolving public attacker IPs and NAT ports to specific subscriber private IPs
ISP subscriber KYC showing physical premises of the bank account hacker
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable IP addresses identified from bank servers or TSP online eSIM portal logs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Positive identification of the ISP subscriber name and physical location of the attacker.
if_blocked: If IP addresses resolve to mobile data networks, route IPDR requisitions through entity_id telecom_operator.

steps.title: Raid, Seizure of SIM Cloning / Swapping Hardware & Arrest
steps.description: Execute search warrants at the physical locations identified via store CCTV, IMEI tracking, telecom CDR, and ISP logs. Arrest the SIM swap gang, corrupt PoS agents, and bank hackers. Seize mobile phones, stolen SIM cards, fake ID manufacturing setups, and laptops.
required_evidence: Seizure memos of mobile handsets, blank SIM cards, forged Aadhaar/PAN cards, printers, and computing devices
Forensic mirror images of computers and phones showing banking credentials and victim databases
Arrest memos and interrogation disclosures
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable physical address and suspect identity established from PoS CCTV, IMEI clustering, or ISP logs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Dismantling of the SIM swap syndicate, arrest of operatives, and submission of digital/physical exhibits to FSL.
if_blocked: If the syndicate operates across interstate borders, coordinate raid execution with State Cyber Cell / CID.

steps.title: Judicial Application for Restitution of Defrauded Funds
steps.description: Submit a formal investigation report and application under BNSS Section 503 before the jurisdictional Magistrate to release frozen funds held in beneficiary bank accounts back to the victim.
required_evidence: Certified schedule of frozen balances in recipient bank accounts
Complainant's verification report and indemnity bond for property release
Investigating Officer's official report endorsing fund restoration
steps.condition_to_start: Defrauded funds successfully frozen in destination bank accounts.
steps.condition_to_complete: Court order directing the banks to release and wire the frozen money to the complainant's account.
if_blocked: If funds were fully withdrawn but police seized cash or vehicles during the raid, move an application before the court to disburse compensation to the victim out of the forfeited assets under BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: The SIM swap was executed using highly sophisticated forged identity documents that bypassed PoS scrutiny, stolen funds were immediately converted to cryptocurrency via P2P traders, and attackers used burner devices.
suggested_actions: Examine the biometric authentication logs at the PoS terminal: if fingerprint authentication was bypassed or faked using silicon clones, report the security breach to UIDAI under entity_id uidai_aadhaar (via High Court order) and DoT for systemic investigation.
Analyse the Call Detail Records (CDR) of the newly activated SIM card during its brief operational window to identify calls made to bank OTP servers, co-conspirators, or test numbers.

File a formal complaint with DoT TERM cell against the telecom operator for violation of mandatory statutory SIM replacement verification guidelines, establishing grounds for civil compensation for the victim.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigating OTP Phishing, Vishing & Social Engineering Account Takeovers
source: Synthesized from I4C investigation checklists, RBI customer protection circulars, and police cyber cell manuals

steps.title: Victim Triage & Social Engineering Vector Profiling
steps.description: Interview the victim to document the exact social engineering modality: vishing phone call (impersonating bank executive/KYC officer/rewards agent), phishing SMS/email link, or screen-sharing malware (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Screen Share). Collect call logs, SMS headers, and screenshots.
required_evidence: Screenshots of phishing SMS / WhatsApp messages showing sender ID and link [1.1.2]
Victim's phone call logs showing incoming vishing phone numbers and call durations
Bank account / wallet statement showing unauthorized transactions
NCRP / CFCFRMS Ticket Acknowledgement Number
steps.condition_to_start: Victim reports unauthorized account takeover and fund transfer after sharing an OTP, clicking a link, or downloading a remote access app.
steps.condition_to_complete: Establishment of the exact compromise vector and compilation of initial communication and banking evidence.
if_blocked: If the victim's phone is currently locked or controlled by remote access malware, immediately power off the device, remove the SIM card, and transfer the handset to FSL for safe forensic triage.

steps.title: Emergency Bank Account & Wallet Freezing
steps.description: Verify the complaint on NCRP / 1930. Issue immediate Section 106 BNSS notices to the beneficiary banks, wallets, or payment aggregators where the stolen funds were transferred. Request debit freeze, account holder KYC, and transaction ledgers.
required_evidence: Certified bank statements and KYC dossiers of Level-1 and Level-2 recipient accounts [1.1.1]
Bank confirmations of debit freeze / lien placement under BNSS Section 106
Internet banking login IP addresses and device fingerprints of recipient accounts
steps.condition_to_start: Beneficiary account numbers, IFSCs, or VPAs identified from victim's transaction alerts or NCRP portal.
steps.condition_to_complete: Freezing of available funds across recipient bank accounts and receipt of account holder KYC.
if_blocked: If funds were routed into merchant e-commerce wallets (e.g., Amazon Pay, Paytm), serve Section 106 freeze notices directly on the e-commerce entities under entity_id ecommerce_platform.

steps.title: Telecom Tracing of Vishing Callers and Phishing SMS Senders
steps.description: Issue notices under BNSS Section 94 to TSPs to trace the phone numbers used to make vishing calls or send phishing SMS. Obtain CAF, CDR with tower locations, and IMEI histories. For bulk SMS phishing, request DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) header registration KYC.
required_evidence: CAF and CDR with Cell ID locations for vishing phone numbers
IMEI tracking history showing handset clustering of telecallers
TRAI DLT registration KYC for bulk SMS sender headers (e.g., VK-SBIBNK, AD-KYCFIL)
steps.condition_to_start: Vishing phone numbers or SMS sender IDs identified from victim's phone logs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of CAF, CDR, IMEI data, and bulk SMS telemarketer KYC from the telecom operator.
if_blocked: If bulk SMS was dispatched via an illegal proxy telemarketer, coordinate with DoT TERM cell to suspend the telemarketer's SIP/SMSC interconnect license.

steps.title: ISP IPDR Tracing of Unauthorized Logins and Phishing Sites
steps.description: Analyse IP addresses obtained from bank internet banking login logs or phishing URL hosting logs. Issue notices to ISPs to obtain IPDR, NAT port binding records, and physical installation addresses of the hackers.
required_evidence: IPDR logs resolving public attacker/login IPs and NAT ports to private subscriber IPs
ISP subscriber KYC showing physical premises of the account takeover hacker
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable IP addresses identified from bank server login logs or CERT-In phishing domain reports.
steps.condition_to_complete: Positive identification of the ISP subscriber name and physical location of the hacker.
if_blocked: If IP addresses resolve to mobile data networks, route IPDR requisitions through entity_id telecom_operator.

steps.title: ATM / PoS CCTV Requisition for Cash Withdrawals
steps.description: If the stolen funds were withdrawn via ATM cash encashment or spent at physical retail PoS stores by mule account holders, immediately issue notices to the acquiring bank for ATM Electronic Journal (EJ) logs and CCTV footage.
required_evidence: Video footage of the ATM kiosk or retail PoS counter covering the exact withdrawal window
ATM Electronic Journal (EJ) transaction logs
steps.condition_to_start: Mule bank account statement confirms physical cash withdrawal via ATM or PoS swipe.
steps.condition_to_complete: Procurement of clear CCTV video clips showing the physical withdrawer.
if_blocked: If ATM CCTV is unavailable, check municipal smart city traffic cameras or nearby commercial establishment cameras under entity_id private_cctv_sources covering the ATM exit routes.

steps.title: Raid, Seizure of Phishing / Vishing Call Centers & Arrest
steps.description: Conduct search and seizure operations at the physical locations identified via telecom CDR, ISP logs, and ATM CCTV. Arrest telecallers, phishing script developers, and money mules. Seize mobile phones, SIM boxes, laptops, registers, and ATM cards.
required_evidence: Seizure memos of computing devices, mobile phones, SIM cards, ATM cards, and telecalling scripts
Forensic mirror images of hard drives showing victim databases, OTP interception scripts, and banking logs
Arrest memos and interrogation disclosures
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable physical address and suspect identity established from telecom, ISP, or CCTV tracing.
steps.condition_to_complete: Dismantling of the phishing/vishing syndicate, arrest of operatives, and submission of digital/physical exhibits to FSL.
if_blocked: If the primary call center operates from an inter-state cybercrime hub (e.g., Jamtara, Mewat, Bharatpur), coordinate raid execution with State Cyber Cell / CID.

steps.title: Judicial Application for Restitution of Defrauded Funds
steps.description: Submit a formal investigation report and application under BNSS Section 503 before the jurisdictional Magistrate to release frozen funds held in beneficiary bank accounts back to the victim.
required_evidence: Certified schedule of frozen balances in recipient bank accounts
Complainant's verification report and indemnity bond for property release
Investigating Officer's official report endorsing fund restoration
steps.condition_to_start: Defrauded funds successfully frozen in destination bank accounts.
steps.condition_to_complete: Court order directing the banks to release and wire the frozen money to the complainant's account.
if_blocked: If the bank refuses to restore funds citing customer negligence (sharing OTP), provide the court with RBI Zero Liability Circular analysis proving systemic banking security lapses or prompt 1930 reporting mitigation.

dead_end_strategies.condition: The vishing call center operated from untraceable pre-activated burner SIM cards, stolen funds were rapidly withdrawn from remote ATMs by masked mules, and digital login IPs were masked behind public Wi-Fi networks.
suggested_actions: Perform IMEI clustering on the mobile handsets used to insert the burner SIM cards; track the historical SIM cards previously used in those same IMEI slots to identify genuine personal numbers of the culprits.
Analyse the point-of-sale (PoS) retailer or Business Correspondent (BC) who activated the cluster of burner SIMs and mule bank accounts; prosecute the fraudulent facilitator under Section 94/96 BNSS.

Check if the victim reported the fraud to 1930 within the 'Golden Hour'; if so, assist the victim in filing a formal claim against the bank before the RBI Banking Ombudsman for failure to implement real-time fraud monitoring.
